//: THE 5C QUESTION SET. This file is the source of truth for the questionnaire.
The questions below are PLACEHOLDERS. The coaching team replaces them; nothing in
the UI, the controllers or the storage layer needs to change when they do.
Rules when editing:
* 'key' is the stable identifier that answers are stored against. Changing a key
orphans every answer already submitted for it. Change 'text' freely; change a
'key' only when you genuinely mean 'this is a different question'.
* Keys must be unique across the whole file, lower-case, and use hyphens.
* Every category needs at least one question. The intended shape is 5 x 5 = 25.
* 'reversed' marks a negatively worded statement. It is scored as (6 - value) so
that a high score always means 'good'. Do not flip the scale in the form to
compensate -- that reverses it twice.
* Three wordings per question, one per reader, all optional except 'text':
text            -- the player, about themselves: 'I keep working ...'
textAboutPlayer -- the coach, about a player:    'The player keeps ...'
textForGuardian -- the guardian, about a child:  'My child keeps ...'
Each falls back to the one above it, so filling in only 'text' still works for
everybody. It is the same statement, the same 1-5 scale, and the answer is
stored identically whichever wording produced it -- only the grammar changes.
Keep the three in step: they should differ in person, not in meaning.
* 'color' marks a category, and every question in it, with one of a fixed set of
names: indigo, teal, plum, rust, moss, sky, sand, slate. A name and not a hex
value -- the content security policy has no unsafe-inline, so a colour that is
not one of these has no class behind it and the app refuses to start.
The marker matters because the FORM NO LONGER GROUPS THE STATEMENTS BY CATEGORY:
all twenty-five are shuffled, so the colour and the category name printed on each
statement are what tell a reader that two of them belong together. A question may
override its category's colour, but normally should not -- twenty-five different
colours is not a code, it is a rainbow. Leaving 'color' out is fine: a category
then gets the palette entry at its own position, which is five distinct markers.
* Red, amber and green are deliberately NOT in the palette. Those three mean a
score band on the coach pages, and a question marked red beside a number coloured
red would read as a verdict on the answer.
The app validates this file at startup and refuses to start with a clear error if
it is malformed, so a typo shows up immediately instead of halfway through a round.

categories.name: Commitment
categories.description: Drive, and the ability to keep working at long-term development.

questions.text: I give high effort throughout training and matches.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player gives high effort throughout training and matches.
questions.textForGuardian: My child puts consistent effort into their football activities.

questions.text: I keep working when I am tired or things become difficult.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player keeps working when tired or when things become difficult.
questions.textForGuardian: My child continues working when tired or when things become difficult.

questions.text: I arrive mentally and physically ready to train and play.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player arrives mentally and physically ready to train and play.
questions.textForGuardian: My child prepares themselves appropriately for training and matches.

questions.text: I take responsibility for completing the things agreed for my own development.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player takes responsibility for completing things agreed for their own development.
questions.textForGuardian: My child takes responsibility for things agreed for their own development.

questions.text: I continue contributing to the team even when I am not directly involved in the play.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player continues contributing to the team even when they are not directly involved in the play.
questions.textForGuardian: My child continues trying to contribute even when they are not directly involved or things are not going their way.

categories.name: Communication
categories.description: Communication with team-mates, opponents, the coaching staff and the support team.

questions.text: I give teammates clear and useful information.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player gives teammates clear and useful information.
questions.textForGuardian: My child communicates useful information to teammates when needed.

questions.text: I listen and respond when teammates or coaches communicate with me.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player listens and responds when teammates or coaches communicate with them.
questions.textForGuardian: My child listens and responds when coaches or teammates communicate with them.

questions.text: I encourage and support teammates when things are difficult or after mistakes.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player encourages and supports teammates when things are difficult or after mistakes.
questions.textForGuardian: My child encourages and supports teammates when things are difficult or after mistakes.

questions.text: I use positive and constructive body language towards others.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player uses positive and constructive body language towards others..
questions.textForGuardian: My child generally uses positive and constructive body language towards others.

questions.text: I communicate what I need or expect from teammates clearly and respectfully.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player communicates what they need or expect from teammates clearly and respectfully.
questions.textForGuardian: My child communicates what they need or expect from others clearly and respectfully.

categories.name: Concentration
categories.description: Holding focus through a full session or match.

questions.text: I keep my attention on the task even when there are distractions.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player keeps their attention on the task even when there are distractions.
questions.textForGuardian: My child is able to stay focused on what they need to do despite distractions.

questions.text: I refocus quickly after mistakes, stoppages or changes in play
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player refocuses quickly after mistakes, stoppages or changes in play.
questions.textForGuardian: My child is able to refocus after mistakes or setbacks.

questions.text: I stay mentally engaged even when exercises are repetitive or I am less involved.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player stays mentally engaged even when exercises are repetitive or they are less involved.
questions.textForGuardian: My child remains mentally engaged even when things become repetitive or they are less involved.

questions.text: I listen carefully when coaches or teammates give important information.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player listens carefully when coaches or teammates give important information.
questions.textForGuardian: My child listens carefully when important information or instructions are given.

questions.text: I remember and apply the focus points we have agreed on.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player remembers and applies agreed focus points.
questions.textForGuardian: My child remembers and tries to apply agreed football-related focus points.

categories.name: Control
categories.description: Self-control and emotional regulation under pressure.

questions.text: I regain my composure quickly after making a mistake.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player regains their composure quickly after making a mistake.
questions.textForGuardian: My child regains their composure after making mistakes.

questions.text: I stay calm enough to respond effectively when I am under pressure.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player stays calm enough to respond effectively when under pressure.
questions.textForGuardian: My child is able to stay sufficiently calm when under pressure.

questions.text: I respond constructively when I become frustrated or disappointed.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player responds constructively when frustrated or disappointed.
questions.textForGuardian: My child responds constructively when frustrated or disappointed.

questions.text: I take responsibility for my reactions rather than blaming others.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player takes responsibility for their reactions rather than blaming others.
questions.textForGuardian: My child takes responsibility for their reactions rather than blaming others.

questions.text: I help teammates regain their composure when they are struggling.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player helps teammates regain their composure when they are struggling.
questions.textForGuardian: My child tries to support teammates when they are frustrated or struggling.

categories.name: Confidence
categories.description: Self-belief and trust in one's own ability in training and matches.

questions.text: I take responsibility and make myself available in difficult situations.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player takes responsibility and makes themselves available in difficult situations.
questions.textForGuardian: My child takes responsibility rather than avoiding difficult situations.

questions.text: I attempt challenging actions even when I am unsure whether they will succeed.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player attempts challenging actions even when they are unsure whether they will succeed.
questions.textForGuardian: My child is willing to attempt challenging things even when they are unsure whether they will succeed.

questions.text: After making a mistake, I get involved again rather than withdrawing.
questions.textAboutPlayer: After making a mistake, the player gets involved again rather than withdrawing.
questions.textForGuardian: After making mistakes or experiencing setbacks, my child is willing to try again.

questions.text: I show belief in my ability when I am under pressure.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player shows belief in their ability when under pressure.
questions.textForGuardian: My child shows belief in their ability when facing pressure or challenges.

questions.text: My body language shows confidence when things are difficult.
questions.textAboutPlayer: The player's body language shows confidence when things are difficult.
questions.textForGuardian: My child's body language generally shows confidence when things are difficult.
